_note: main idea — 학교생활 대화. 두 사람이 주고받는 중에 요지가 서서히 드러나게 쓴다.
1) 오답 3개는 전부 '음원에 실제로 언급된' 세부사항으로 만든다. 언급조차 없는 내용을
오답으로 넣으면 주제 파악이 아니라 단순 기억력 문제가 된다.
아이가 '들어본 것 같은데?'에서 걸려야 진짜 main idea 문항이다.
2) 주제를 첫 문장에 넣지 않는다. 읽기와 달리 듣기는 되돌아갈 수 없어서,
첫 줄에 답이 있으면 나머지 40초가 무의미해진다.

turns.t: Did you get the study room for Thursday?
No. They were all booked by seven in the morning.
Seven! Who books a room at seven?
The ninth graders, apparently. So I looked around instead.
And?
The art room is empty after lunch on Thursdays. Ms. Han said we can use it if we put the chairs back.
That's better than the study room anyway. More space.

items.stem: What are the students mainly discussing?
choices: How early the ninth graders wake up
Why Ms. Han moved her class
How to book a study room online
Finding another place to study
items.explanation: 예약 실패와 9학년 이야기는 배경이고, 대화의 중심은 '대신 쓸 다른 공간을 찾았다'는 해결이다.

turns.t: Who should run last in the relay?
Jiwon, obviously. She's the fastest.
That's what everyone says. But last year we put our fastest runner last and still lost.
Because we were already too far behind by then.
Right. If the fastest runner goes first, we start ahead, and nobody has to catch up.
Hm. So the order matters as much as who's on the team.
That's the whole point I'm making.

items.stem: What is the main point of the conversation?
choices: Jiwon is the fastest runner in the class
The team lost the relay last year
Everyone should get a turn in the relay
Running order can decide the race, not just speed
items.explanation: 지원의 실력과 작년 패배는 근거로 든 사례다. 요지는 마지막 두 줄의 '누가 뛰느냐 못지않게 순서가 중요하다'이다.

turns.t: The lunch waste campaign isn't working.
We put posters in every hallway.
I know. And the bins are just as full as before.
Maybe people don't read posters.
Or maybe the problem isn't that they don't care. I watched yesterday. The servers put the same amount on every tray.
Oh. So a small kid gets the same rice as a ninth grader.
And throws half of it away. Let people choose their portion and the posters won't matter.

items.stem: What does the girl conclude?
choices: Students throw food away because they do not care
The real cause is fixed serving sizes, not attitude
The posters should be moved to the cafeteria
Younger students eat less than older students
items.explanation: 포스터와 학년별 식사량은 논의 과정이고, 결론은 '태도가 아니라 똑같이 퍼 주는 배식 방식이 원인'이라는 것이다.

turns.t: You've been holding that exchange program form for a week.
I keep starting it and stopping.
Is it the language? Your English is strong enough.
It's not that. It's six months. My grandmother lives with us, and she's not well.
Ah. So it isn't whether you can. It's whether you want to be away right now.
Yeah. And nobody's been asking me that part.
Then let's talk about that part.

items.stem: What is the conversation mainly about?
choices: Whether the student's English is good enough
The real reason the student is hesitating
How long the exchange program lasts
The student's grandmother's health
items.explanation: 영어 실력은 교사가 먼저 배제했고 기간과 할머니는 이유의 일부다. 대화의 중심은 아무도 묻지 않았던 '진짜 망설임의 이유'가 드러나는 과정이다.

turns.t: For the school paper, I want to write about the new vending machines.
That's it? People will read two lines and stop.
Everyone uses them, though.
Sure, but here's the thing. The money from those machines goes somewhere. Nobody knows where.
...Huh. I never thought about that.
Same topic. But now there's a question in it.
Okay, that I'd read.

items.stem: What is the boy's main advice?
choices: The vending machines are too expensive
The school paper needs more readers
A story needs a question, not just a familiar topic
They should write about something else entirely
items.explanation: 자판기 자체는 그대로 두라고 했으므로 주제 변경이 아니다. 요지는 '같은 소재라도 궁금증이 있어야 읽힌다'이다.

turns.t: The art supply list came out. It's twenty thousand won.
For one project?
Canvas, paint, brushes. I asked Ms. Yoon if there was a cheaper way.
What did she say?
She said the assignment is about texture, not materials. Cardboard, fabric scraps, old buttons - all fine.
So we could just use things from home.
She actually said those might work better.

items.stem: What did the students learn?
choices: The art project costs twenty thousand won
Ms. Yoon changed the assignment
Canvas is better than cardboard for texture
The project can be done with materials from home
items.explanation: 과제가 바뀐 것이 아니라 재료 조건이 원래 자유로웠다는 것이 핵심이다. 금액은 문제 제기의 계기일 뿐이다.

turns.t: I did almost all of the group project again.
Did you tell the teacher?
And say what? 'They didn't help'? It's my word against three people.
So what are you going to do next time?
Write it down. On day one, we split the parts and everyone signs next to their name.
That feels a bit formal for a class project.
Maybe. But then nobody has to argue about who did what at the end. It's just there on paper.

items.stem: What is the girl's main idea?
choices: Her group members were lazy this time
Teachers should grade group work differently
Group projects should be done alone
Writing down roles in advance prevents the argument later
items.explanation: 불평에서 시작하지만 대화의 무게는 '다음엔 어떻게 할 것인가'로 옮겨간다. 요지는 처음에 역할을 문서로 정해 두면 나중에 다툴 일이 없다는 것.

turns.t: Your error notebook is very neat.
Thank you. I copy the correct solution for every problem I miss.
I can see that. How many of these have you missed twice?
...A few. Maybe more than a few.
Copying the answer teaches your hand, not your head. Cover the solution and solve it again from the start.
Even the ones I understand now?
Especially those. Understanding an answer and producing one are different things.

items.stem: What is the teacher's main point?
choices: The notebook should be neater
Redoing the problem beats copying the answer
The student misses too many problems
Error notebooks are not useful
items.explanation: '정답을 베끼면 손만 배운다'와 마지막 문장이 요지다. 노트가 지저분하다거나 오답이 많다는 지적이 아니다.

turns.t: I signed up for the cooking class after school.
Not the writing workshop? Your essay grades are the problem, aren't they?
That's exactly why I didn't pick it. I already do essays all day.
So you picked the fun one.
I picked the one I'll actually show up to. Last term I signed up for math club and quit in three weeks.
...Okay, that's fair.
A class you attend beats a better class you skip.

items.stem: What is the boy mainly arguing?
choices: Cooking is more useful than writing
His essay grades do not matter
Math club was badly run
Choosing something he will stick with matters more
items.explanation: 마지막 문장이 요지다. 요리가 더 유용하다는 주장이 아니라 '끝까지 나갈 수업이 더 낫다'는 것.

turns.t: Our class library is a mess. Should we sort by author?
Nobody looks up authors. I've never heard anyone say 'do we have anything by so-and-so'.
By color, then? It would look nice.
Looks nice, finds nothing.
Okay, what do people actually ask for?
'Something scary.' 'Something short.' 'Something funny.'
...So we sort by that. Scary, short, funny.

items.stem: What do the students decide?
choices: To sort the books by color for a nicer look
To organize the books the way people actually ask for them
To sort the books by author's name
To get rid of the class library
items.explanation: 작가별·색깔별은 검토했다가 버린 안이다. 결론은 '사람들이 실제로 찾는 방식'대로 분류하자는 것.

turns.t: For volunteer hours, there's the animal shelter across the city or the daycare next door.
The shelter sounds better.
It's an hour and a half each way.
Oh.
My sister did that last year. She went twice and then stopped. Three hours of travel for two hours of work.
So the daycare, even if it's less exciting.
The one you keep going back to is the one that helps.

items.stem: What is the main point?
choices: The animal shelter needs more volunteers
His sister was not committed enough
A place you can keep returning to is worth more
Daycare work is more valuable than shelter work
items.explanation: 누나의 사례는 근거이고, 어린이집 일이 더 가치 있다는 주장도 아니다. 요지는 '계속 갈 수 있는 곳이 실제로 도움이 된다'이다.

turns.t: I memorized my whole presentation. Word for word.
All four minutes?
All four minutes. But when Ms. Park asked a question in the middle, I completely lost my place.
What did you do?
Started over from the beginning. In front of everyone.
Oof.
Next time I'm learning the five main ideas and just talking. If I know it, I can pick it back up anywhere.

items.stem: What did the girl learn?
choices: Presentations should be shorter than four minutes
Ms. Park should not interrupt presentations
She needs more practice before presenting
Knowing the ideas is safer than memorizing the words
items.explanation: 길이나 교사의 질문이 문제가 아니라 '통째로 외운 방식' 자체가 문제였다는 깨달음이 요지다.

turns.t: How did the history test go?
Badly. I studied for six hours.
Six hours is a lot.
The night before. All six of them, the night before.
Ah.
By the last chapter I couldn't remember the first one. Same six hours over six days would have been a completely different test.

items.stem: What is the girl's main point?
choices: The history test was unfairly hard
She did not study long enough
Spreading the same study time out would have worked better
She should have studied a different chapter
items.explanation: 공부 시간이 부족했던 게 아니라 하루에 몰아넣은 것이 문제였다는 것이 요지다.

turns.t: Here's the club poster. Meeting times, room number, what we do, who to contact, and the history of the club.
That's a lot of words for a hallway.
People need to know all of it.
They walk past in four seconds. What do they need in four seconds?
...The name. And when to show up.
Put those in big letters. Everything else goes on the paper you hand them when they come.

items.stem: What is the boy suggesting?
choices: The club should meet at a different time
The poster should carry only what fits in four seconds
The club's history is not interesting
They should hand out papers instead of posting
items.explanation: 나머지 정보를 버리라는 게 아니라 '포스터에는 4초 안에 읽히는 것만, 나머지는 유인물로'라는 배치 조언이다.

turns.t: You asked to move seats. Where would you like to sit?
Next to Junho, if that's okay.
You sat next to Junho in September. You asked to move away.
...I did.
Why the change?
Back then I couldn't concentrate because we talked too much. But my grades went down after I moved, not up.
So the talking wasn't the problem.
I think I was just bored. Junho asks me things I have to actually think about.

items.stem: What does the boy come to realize?
choices: He should not sit near his friends
Junho distracts him from his work
The talking was not what hurt his grades
The teacher assigned him a bad seat
items.explanation: 자리를 옮긴 뒤에도 성적이 떨어졌다는 사실에서 '수다가 원인이 아니었다'는 결론이 나온다. 마지막 줄이 그 반전을 확인해 준다.

turns.t: We only have two practices left before the cheering contest.
And half the class still doesn't know the second part.
Should we add a practice at lunch?
People won't come. They've got other things.
Then what?
Cut the second part. Do the first part really well instead of two parts badly.
The judges won't know what we cut.

items.stem: What do they decide to do?
choices: Add extra practice during lunch
Ask the judges for more time
Teach the second part again tomorrow
Shorten the routine so they can do it well
items.explanation: 점심 연습은 제안했다가 접었다. 결론은 '두 부분을 어설프게 하느니 한 부분을 잘하자'는 것.

turns.t: Your book report is a very good summary.
Thank you.
That wasn't quite a compliment. I asked what you thought of the book.
But I wrote what happens in it.
You did. I could learn the plot from the back cover, though. I can't learn from anywhere else what you made of it.
So... less story, more me.
Two sentences of story. The rest is you.

items.stem: What is the teacher asking for?
choices: A longer report
A more accurate summary of the plot
The student's own response rather than the plot
A different book to be chosen
items.explanation: 줄거리를 정확히 쓰라거나 길게 쓰라는 요구가 아니다. '줄거리는 뒤표지에도 있다'는 말이 요지를 압축한다.

turns.t: The student council wants to ban phones during lunch.
Everyone will hate that.
That's what I said. So I asked why they proposed it.
And?
Two of them eat alone every day. They said nobody talks anymore.
Oh.
The rule is probably the wrong answer. But the thing behind it is real.

items.stem: What is the boy mainly saying?
choices: The phone ban should be approved
The proposal comes from a real problem even if the rule is wrong
The student council does not listen to students
Students should eat lunch together
items.explanation: 규칙에는 반대하면서도 그 뒤의 문제는 진짜라고 말한다. 마지막 두 문장이 그 균형을 정확히 담고 있다.

turns.t: The classroom plant is dying again.
But we water it every day. It's on the duty list.
That's the problem. Six people are on the list, and all six water it.
...Every day?
Every day. The soil never dries out.
So we're drowning it by being responsible.
One person, twice a week. That's all it needs.

items.stem: What is the main idea?
choices: The plant needs a sunnier spot
Students forget their duty too often
The duty list should have more names
Too much watering, not too little, is killing the plant
items.explanation: 돌보지 않아서가 아니라 여섯 명이 각자 물을 주어 과습이 된 것이 원인이다. 예상을 뒤집는 구조.

turns.t: Your career survey says medicine. Twice you've written 'my parents think so' in the margin.
They're not forcing me.
I didn't say they were. What did you do last Saturday?
...Fixed my neighbor's bike. And then two more bikes because word got around.
Four hours, unpaid, on a Saturday.
It's not a career, though.
I'm not telling you to become a mechanic. I'm telling you that what you choose to do when nobody assigns it is information. Don't throw it away.

items.stem: What is the teacher's main message?
choices: The student should become a bicycle mechanic
What he does freely is evidence worth considering
Medicine is the wrong choice for him
His parents should not influence his choice
items.explanation: 교사는 정비사가 되라고 한 적이 없다고 직접 부정한다. 요지는 '아무도 시키지 않았는데 하는 일은 정보다'라는 마지막 문장.

turns.t: Everyone wants to be in a group with their friends for the school trip.
Naturally.
But last year the two biggest friend groups took one room each, and four people were left over.
I remember. They didn't talk to anyone the whole trip.
So this year, groups of four, and every group needs at least one person from a different class.
Some people will complain.
For about a day. Then nobody's left standing alone.

items.stem: What is the boy proposing?
choices: That friends should not travel together
A grouping rule so nobody is left out
That the trip should be canceled
Larger groups of six or more
items.explanation: 친구끼리 못 다니게 하자는 것이 아니라, 남는 사람이 없도록 조 구성에 조건을 붙이자는 제안이다.

turns.t: For the festival booth, how about a haunted house?
In a classroom, with the lights on and the door open?
We could cover the windows.
With what, and when? We get the room at eight and the festival starts at ten.
Two hours isn't much.
Whatever we pick has to be built in two hours by six people. That rules out most of the fun ideas.
Then let's start from what fits, not from what sounds best.

items.stem: What do they conclude?
choices: A haunted house would be the most popular booth
The classroom is too small for a booth
The idea must fit the time and people they have
They should ask for the room earlier
items.explanation: 귀신의 집이 좋은지 나쁜지가 아니라 '2시간·6명이라는 조건에 맞는 것부터 고르자'는 결론이 요지다.

turns.t: Our English study group met four times and then died.
What went wrong?
Nothing dramatic. We planned two hours every Saturday. The first week everyone came. By week four it was me and Sujin.
Two hours is a big ask on a weekend.
That's what I think now. Fifteen minutes every morning before class would have been easier to keep.
Less time overall, though.
Less time that actually happens beats more time that doesn't.

items.stem: What is the boy's main point?
choices: A small routine that survives beats an ambitious one that fails
Saturday is a bad day for meetings
The group needed more members
Sujin was the only committed member
items.explanation: 요일이나 인원 문제가 아니라 '지속 가능한 크기'가 요지다. 마지막 문장이 이를 압축한다.

turns.t: Someone left a jacket in the gym again.
The lost and found box is completely full.
And almost nothing gets claimed. I checked - out of thirty items, four have names in them.
Four out of thirty?
And all four of those went home in a week. The other twenty-six are still sitting there.
So the box isn't the problem.
A name tag is thirty seconds of work.

items.stem: What is the girl's main point?
choices: Labeling items is what actually gets them returned
Students are careless with their belongings
The lost and found box needs to be bigger
The gym should be checked more often
items.explanation: 30개 중 이름이 있는 4개만 돌아갔다는 대비가 근거이고, 요지는 '이름표를 붙이는 것이 실제로 효과가 있다'는 것.

turns.t: For the choir contest, everyone wants the hard piece.
It's more impressive.
If we sing it well. We have five weeks and the high part is out of range for half the altos.
They could practice.
They could. Or we sing the simpler piece so well that people get goosebumps.
Hm. Last year's winners did the easiest song in the whole contest.
Exactly. Nobody remembered it was easy.

items.stem: What is the main point of the conversation?
choices: The altos need more practice
A piece performed well matters more than a difficult one
Last year's contest was judged unfairly
Five weeks is not enough time to prepare
items.explanation: 알토 음역과 작년 우승은 근거다. 요지는 '어려운 곡보다 잘 부른 곡이 남는다'이며 마지막 줄이 이를 확인한다.

turns.t: You didn't wear goggles during the acid demonstration.
I was only watching. I wasn't touching anything.
Neither was the student who got splashed in my class four years ago. He was three meters away, watching.
The rule isn't about what you're doing. It's about what the room is doing.
I didn't think of it that way.
Most people don't, until they have to.

items.stem: What is the teacher's main point?
choices: Safety rules cover everyone in the room, not just the person working
The student should apologize to the class
Acid demonstrations are too dangerous for students
The student was not paying attention
items.explanation: 4년 전 사고는 근거로 든 사례다. 요지는 '규칙은 네가 무엇을 하느냐가 아니라 그 공간에서 무슨 일이 일어나느냐의 문제'라는 것.

turns.t: I have forty photos for the exhibition and only six spots.
Pick your six best.
That's what I tried. But my six best don't go together at all. A sunset, a shoe, my dog, a building...
Then it's forty separate pictures, just fewer of them.
Right. So maybe six that are only pretty good, but all about the same thing.
Like all the rain ones.
Those aren't my best. But together they'd actually say something.

items.stem: What does the girl decide?
choices: To choose photos that work together over individually strong ones
To display her six strongest photos
To ask for more display space
To take new photos before the exhibition
items.explanation: '가장 잘 찍은 6장'은 시도했다가 버린 방향이다. 결론은 개별 완성도보다 하나로 묶이는 구성을 택하겠다는 것.

turns.t: I've been late four times this month.
Get a louder alarm.
I have three alarms. I turn all of them off in my sleep.
What time do you go to bed?
Around one. Sometimes later.
So the alarm isn't the problem.
Yeah. I've been trying to fix the morning when the trouble starts the night before.

items.stem: What does the boy realize?
choices: He needs a louder alarm clock
He should leave the house earlier
The real cause is his bedtime, not his alarm
Being late is not a serious problem
items.explanation: 알람 3개를 이미 쓰고 있다는 점이 알람 가설을 무너뜨린다. 요지는 마지막 문장의 '아침이 아니라 전날 밤이 문제'다.

turns.t: Can I copy your notes from Tuesday? I was absent.
Sure. Fair warning, they might not help much.
Why not? Your notes are famous.
They're short because I write down what I didn't already know. Half of Tuesday I just listened.
So the parts you skipped might be exactly the parts I need.
Probably. Take them, but sit with me at lunch and I'll fill in the gaps.

items.stem: What is the main idea?
choices: The boy's notes are badly organized
Someone else's notes reflect what they needed, not what you need
The girl should not have been absent
Notes are more useful than listening
items.explanation: 필기가 부실해서가 아니라 '그 사람이 몰랐던 것만 적혀 있어서' 남에게는 안 맞는다는 것이 요지다.

turns.t: Team captains pick players again today.
And the same two people get picked last again.
Every single time. It's been like that since March.
What if the teacher just counted us off? One, two, one, two.
Teams would be less even.
A little. But nobody would have to stand there while everyone looks away.
Yeah. That trade is worth it.

items.stem: What are the students mainly discussing?
choices: A fairer way to form teams
Which students are the best athletes
How to make the teams more evenly matched
Whether the teacher should join the game
items.explanation: 전력 균형은 오히려 조금 포기하겠다고 했다. 대화의 중심은 '마지막까지 남는 사람이 없게 하는 방식'이다.

turns.t: You said you'd hate this book and you finished it in two days.
I know.
I've recommended you six books and you didn't open any of them.
Because you kept saying they were beautiful and important.
They are.
This one you just said 'there's a guy trapped on a train and nobody believes him.' That I wanted to know the end of.
So I should stop telling you books are good and start telling you what happens.

items.stem: What does the girl learn about recommending books?
choices: Describing the hook works better than praising the book
Her friend does not enjoy reading
She should recommend shorter books
The six earlier books were poor choices
items.explanation: 앞선 6권이 나쁜 책이라는 말은 없다. 요지는 '좋다고 말하기보다 무슨 일이 벌어지는지 말하라'는 마지막 줄이다.

turns.t: Half the lettuce in the school garden died.
We watered it. I have the chart.
Look at where the dead ones are, though. All along the south fence.
That's the sunny side. Shouldn't that be better?
For tomatoes. Lettuce wilts in full afternoon sun.
So we planted the wrong thing in the wrong spot.
Next season the lettuce goes north and the tomatoes go south.

items.stem: What is the main point?
choices: The students forgot to water the garden
The south fence gets too little sunlight
Different plants need different amounts of sun
The garden should be moved elsewhere
items.explanation: 물을 준 기록이 있으므로 관리 부족이 아니고, 남쪽은 햇빛이 강한 쪽이다. 요지는 작물마다 필요한 일조량이 다르다는 것.

turns.t: How did the class meeting go?
Fine. We voted and it was almost unanimous.
Almost. How many people spoke before the vote?
...Four. Maybe five.
Out of twenty-eight.
The rest agreed, though. They raised their hands.
Or they hadn't heard anything worth disagreeing with yet. A vote that fast usually means the quiet people never got in.
So next time we ask before we vote, not after.

items.stem: What is the teacher pointing out?
choices: A quick, near-unanimous vote can hide unheard opinions
The class made the wrong decision
Twenty-eight is too many for one meeting
The student should have led the discussion better
items.explanation: 결정 내용이 틀렸다는 말은 없다. 요지는 '빠르고 만장일치에 가까운 표결은 조용한 사람들이 끼지 못했다는 뜻일 수 있다'는 것.

turns.t: Which scene are you writing about for the film review?
The big chase at the end. It's the best part.
It's also the part everyone will write about.
Because it's the best part.
Ms. Lee has to read thirty of those. What about the scene where he puts the letter down without opening it?
That's ten seconds long.
And it's the reason the chase matters. Nobody else will notice it.

items.stem: What is the girl suggesting?
choices: A smaller, overlooked scene is worth writing about
The chase scene is poorly made
The review should cover the whole film
Ms. Lee prefers shorter reviews
items.explanation: 추격 장면이 못 만들었다는 말은 없다. 요지는 '아무도 주목하지 않는 짧은 장면이 오히려 쓸 거리가 된다'는 제안이다.

turns.t: My vacation plan: learn guitar, read ten books, run every morning, and finish the science kit.
In three weeks?
I made the same list last winter.
How much of it did you do?
None of it. I looked at the list every day and felt bad, and then I stopped looking at the list.
So do fewer things.
One thing. If I can play three chords by September, that's a real summer.

items.stem: What does the boy conclude?
choices: Vacation is too short for any projects
He should have started the list earlier
One achievable goal beats a long list
Learning guitar is harder than it looks
items.explanation: 지난 겨울 실패담이 근거이고, 결론은 '한 가지만 제대로 하는 게 낫다'는 마지막 줄이다.
